description:
User approved in JSON's session, verbatim "yes" (relayed by JSON, 2026-11-19). Source: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-json-four-proposals.html, item P1. Builder: Callables, queued behind its current work (JSON no longer needs it: fz-nml.25 deleted the union).
A dispatch plan already carries DoesNotHold proofs for every clause after one whose pattern missed. Example: integer_step(:overflow, ...) first, then integer_step(acc, _d, 1) when acc > 922337203685477580. After clause 1 misses, the plan proves s0 is not :overflow, and the later clause bodies are typed int. But the guard still compares s0 as the union ValueRef: prim.rs's 'One side unboxed and the other dynamic' path calls fz_value_cmp_raw_const, about 219 instructions per evaluation (cmp 59, TermComparator::compare 71, compare_values 36, AnyValue::from_ref 31, decode_parts 22).
Fix: the guard evaluator reads the subject's type at that point in the dispatch, narrowed by the miss proofs, so the guard lowers to an unbox and an icmp.
Not fz-sc8.240 (narrowed a clause body by a guard call's domain; this is its sibling, per Callables) and not fz-sc8.198 (drops the boolean test of a closed guard type).
Acceptance: an oracle fixture whose later clause guards a subject that earlier clauses narrowed matches Elixir on interp, run and build, and its loop makes no fz_value_cmp_raw_const call.
title: A guard subject is narrowed by what earlier clauses' patterns ruled out
